title: Bollywood Box Office Disappoints, Tech Giants Face Scrutiny, and Social Trends Impact Business
summary: The highly anticipated "Ramayana" movie faced a lackluster opening at the box office, generating mixed reactions and reigniting debates on cinematic expectations. Meanwhile, tech mogul Elon Musk drew attention for his political spending and subsequent social media activity following election losses. Blinkit announced a significant policy change, introducing charges for non-emergency ambulance services due to misuse. The digital landscape saw Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement break social media records and Mr. Beast expand his YouTube empire, while a viral meme unexpectedly caused substantial losses for fashion businesses.
article:
In a week marked by diverse developments across entertainment, technology, and social spheres, several key narratives unfolded, capturing public attention and sparking significant discussion. From box office performances to policy changes and viral phenomena, the landscape of news remained dynamic.

### Bollywood Box Office & Cinematic Debuts

The cinematic release of "Ramayana" has garnered considerable attention, though not entirely for positive reasons. Despite reportedly receiving favorable reviews, the film's opening day box office collection in India was approximately ₹65 crores net, with a gross collection of ₹78 crores. This figure falls significantly short of expectations, failing to surpass the day-one collections of blockbusters like "Pathaan" and "Animal." The performance drew comparisons to "Adipurush," which, despite widespread criticism, achieved a worldwide gross of ₹140 crores on its opening day. With "Ramayana" reportedly made on a budget of ₹125 crores, its initial collections have been deemed disappointing by many, leading to online discussions about audience preferences. Conflicting reports emerged regarding its performance, with some claiming a day-one collection of ₹155 crores, challenging the initial lower estimates.

### Reality Television & Influencer Dynamics

The world of reality television and social media personalities continued to generate buzz. In "Scout," a contestant's interactions with his mother and fellow participant Love Gill became a focal point. Scout's mother reportedly advised him to follow Kashvi's positive guidance, particularly concerning controversial relationships. Scout, however, expressed reluctance, fearing that acknowledging Kashvi's advice would validate external accusations. This led to a public disagreement with Love Gill, stemming from a perceived joke that Scout disliked, escalating into an argument about communication and mutual respect.

Separately, the voice-over artist for "Bigg Boss," Vijay Vikram, addressed fan complaints regarding contestant Qazi's limited screen time. Vijay Vikram clarified that as a voice-over artist, he has no control over editorial or creative decisions concerning screen time, attributing these choices to the show's editors. He urged fans to direct their feedback to Colors' official channels rather than his comment sections, emphasizing that "Bigg Boss" is a game show, not a personal narrative.

### Celebrity Reactions & Legal Developments

Bollywood action star Vidyut Jammwal recently reacted to the viral "someone should run away" meme, which gained traction after a comment by Tiger Shroff. During a podcast appearance, Jammwal expressed amusement at being part of the meme wave, noting how it resonated with people's everyday frustrations, such as feeling overlooked for promotions. He found the creativity surrounding the meme enjoyable and even reposted some iterations himself.

In other news, UK Surseven Rider, a prominent figure, was released from jail after being arrested on allegations of assaulting his brother-in-law. His bail had initially been rejected, but he was seen driving a Lamborghini in an Instagram story, playing a song in the background, signaling his release. He later posted a meme referencing "the top two most dangerous things in Dehradun," which appeared to be a local inside joke.

### Social & Environmental Initiatives

Bittoo Disaster, known for his river cleaning efforts, revealed a concerning deterioration in his health. His prolonged exposure to polluted water during his mission has led to skin infections, constant itching, and pain in his hands and feet. Despite taking medication and precautions, his commitment to cleaning rivers remains unwavering. However, many users online have urged him to prioritize his health, recommending the use of protective gear and avoiding direct contact with waste to prevent further health complications.

### Media Personalities & Public Discourse

Kunal Kamra, a comedian and public commentator, revisited his viral confrontation with journalist Arnab Goswami on a flight. Kamra re-uploaded the video, recalling how he continuously challenged Goswami for two minutes without eliciting a reaction. Kamra criticized Goswami, stating that while he projects fearlessness on camera, confronting someone face-to-face requires genuine courage, unlike the curated environment of a television studio. Kamra asserted that Goswami was and would remain a "coward," particularly when his government patronage and perks diminish.

### Bollywood Controversies & Cultural Debates

Bollywood actor Salman Khan faced backlash for his new song "Your Sexy Beauty" from the patriotic movie "Matrubhoomi." Critics questioned the song's title and lyrics within the context of a patriotic film. The song's composer, Sajid Khan, defended the track, explaining that while Salman Khan initially felt it didn't fit the film's theme and suggested lyric changes, he ultimately decided to include it due to its appeal.

This incident also brought back memories of the "Besharam Rang" controversy involving Deepika Padukone's orange dress from "Pathaan." A BJP MLA issued a warning to Shahrukh Khan regarding his upcoming film, accusing him and others of being "jihadis" who profit by defaming India. The MLA specifically criticized the use of saffron-colored attire in intense dance sequences, threatening protests if scenes were not altered.

### Business Innovations & Partnerships

Food Farmer, a company specializing in protein shakes, announced a significant partnership with PVR Inox. This collaboration will make their "Only What's Kneaded" protein shakes available in PVR Inox theaters, aiming to increase accessibility to healthy beverage options. The company's founder expressed gratitude for the milestone, noting that the protein shakes would be priced at ₹280, making them competitive with other soft drink options. This initiative is currently an experiment, with plans for broader expansion if successful.

### Global Sports & Digital Milestones

In global sports, football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football in an emotional video, which rapidly broke social media records. The video garnered over 33 million likes, 3 million comments, and 6 million shares within a day. Ronaldo departs from international football holding significant records, including the most international matches (234) and the most international goals (146).

On the digital front, YouTube sensation Mr. Beast achieved another remarkable milestone, with his seventh channel surpassing 10 million subscribers. Additionally, his "Beast Animation" channel also crossed the 10 million subscriber mark, further solidifying his expansive digital footprint.

### Tech Moguls & Policy Shifts

Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, faced scrutiny for his involvement in the US midterm elections. Reports indicated that Musk had spent approximately ₹4,700 crores supporting a particular party. He had openly tweeted "Vote Red," urging support for Republicans. Following the party's loss in the elections, Musk promptly deleted his tweet and later posted a humorous remark: "Guess my election interfering Space Lasers didn't work this time."

Blinkit, the quick commerce platform, announced a significant change to its ambulance service. Due to widespread misuse, the company will now charge ₹2,500 for non-emergency transfers. For years, this service had been entirely free, serving over 20,000 emergency and 42,000 non-emergency cases. The company stated that the free service was being exploited for routine check-ups and non-urgent situations, leading to the new policy. However, emergency transfers will continue to be provided free of charge.

### Societal Trends & Economic Impacts

A viral incident in Nagpur showcased a heated exchange between a citizen and a public official. Upon entering an official's office without an appointment, the citizen challenged the official's question about his appointment, asserting that public servants are "servants" of the public.

In a bizarre political development, a losing politician demanded refunds from voters. After failing to win elections, he claimed to have lent ₹1,000 each to nearly 400 people who, he alleged, took the money but did not vote for him. He demanded either a refund or a donation to a local temple, threatening protests outside their homes. His party subsequently suspended him for anti-party activities.

Finally, a seemingly innocuous viral meme of a red and white checkered shirt had an unexpected and detrimental impact on businesses. The shirt became so popular that it was widely worn, leading to a perception of it being "common" or "bad." This trend caused significant losses for businesses that had stocked the shirt as a "hero product" for Diwali, turning substantial inventory into dead stock. Traders expressed frustration, highlighting how a simple meme could disrupt an entire fashion season and impact livelihoods.
